Rashi on Shabbat 108b:10:1.hebrew: מהו למימץ ולמפתח - לשון "אין מעמצין את המת" (לקמן שבת דף קנא:) — עוצם עיניו. כשהוא רוחץ מהן בשבת, מהו שיסגיר ויפתח עיניו כדי שיכנס מהן לעין:
Rashi on Shabbat 108b:10:1.english: What [is the law] regarding closing and opening - [This is] an expression [as in] "one may not close [the eyes of] the deceased" (later, Shabbat 151b) — closing his eyes. When he washes with them on Shabbat, what [is the law] regarding whether he may shut and open his eyes so that [some] of them enter the eye?

Rashi on Shabbat 108b:10:10.hebrew: אפילו על גב עין אסור - דמוכחא מילתא דלרפואה, דאילו לרחיצה מאיס. להכי נקט רוק תפל, לפי שהוא חזק ומרפא:
Rashi on Shabbat 108b:10:10.english: Even on the eye, it is prohibited - For it is evident that [it is] for healing, since for washing it is repulsive. That is why [the Gemara] specifies bland saliva — because it is strong and heals.

Rashi on Shabbat 108b:10:2.hebrew: כיוצא בו שמעתי - דהיכא דמוכחא מילתא דלרפואה עביד, אסור, ומימץ ומפתח נמי מוכחא מילתא. והא אסהדותא דרב דימי דאמר לא טבע גברא בימא דסדום, נפקא לן מינה הא: כיון דמליחי טובא, מסו, ואסר למימץ ולמפתח:
Rashi on Shabbat 108b:10:2.english: A similar case I heard - For wherever it is evident that one is acting for healing, it is prohibited; and [with regard to] closing and opening [one's eyes], it is also evident. And [as for] that testimony of Rav Dimi, who said that a person does not sink in the Sea of Sodom, this emerges from it: since [its waters] are very salty, they heal, and it is prohibited to close and open [one's eyes in them].

Rashi on Shabbat 108b:10:3.hebrew: זימנין א"ל וכו' - שקבל משניהם:
Rashi on Shabbat 108b:10:3.english: Sometimes he said it, etc. - For he received [it] from both of them.

Rashi on Shabbat 108b:10:4.english: And both of them - Rav Mattana and Mar Ukva.

Rashi on Shabbat 108b:10:5.hebrew: משמיה דאבוה דשמואל ולוי אמרי - תרתי מילי אמור, חדא משמיה דאבוה דשמואל וחדא משמיה דלוי:
Rashi on Shabbat 108b:10:5.english: In the name of Shmuel’s father and Levi they say - They said two things: one in the name of Shmuel’s father and one in the name of Levi.

Rashi on Shabbat 108b:10:6.english: One said - Either Shmuel's father or Levi.

Rashi on Shabbat 108b:10:7.hebrew: יין בתוך העין - דעמיץ ופתח, אסור, דמוכחא מילתא:
Rashi on Shabbat 108b:10:7.english: Wine inside the eye - When one closes and opens [his eyes], it is prohibited, because the matter is evident [that it is for healing].

Rashi on Shabbat 108b:10:8.english: On the eye, [it is] permitted - For [people] say they are doing [it] merely for washing.

Rashi on Shabbat 108b:10:9.english: Bland saliva - [Saliva of one] who has not tasted anything since he awoke from his sleep.

Rashi on Shabbat 108b:11:1.hebrew: וליטעמיך כו' - א"כ, לוי ולא חדא אמר? בתמיה, והא חדא משמיה אתמר כדאמרן:
Rashi on Shabbat 108b:11:1.english: And according to your reasoning, etc. - If so, did Levi not say even one [statement]? [This is asked] in astonishment — for indeed one [statement] was stated in his name, as we said [earlier].

Rashi on Shabbat 108b:12:3.hebrew: ונותן ע"ג עיניו - דלדידיה, כיון דאצרכוה לשרותה מע"ש, איכא היכרא וליכא למיגזר. ומאן דחזינהו סבר דרחיצה בעלמא היא, דכסבר שהוא יין:
Rashi on Shabbat 108b:12:3.english: And places [it] on his eyes - For as for him, since [the Sages] required him to soak it on Shabbat eve, there is a distinguishing reminder and there is no [reason] to issue a decree. And whoever sees them thinks that it is mere washing, for he thinks that it is wine.

Rashi on Shabbat 108b:12:4.english: All of this [he] certainly did not permit - For the matter is evident [that it is for healing].

Rashi on Shabbat 108b:12:5.hebrew: מר עוקבא הוה שכיח גבי מר שמואל, ואב ב"ד היה בימיו, כדאמרינן לעיל (שבת דף נה. ובמועד קטן דף טז.):
Rashi on Shabbat 108b:12:5.english: Mar Ukva was frequently with Mar Shmuel, and was head of the court [Av Beit Din] in his days, as we said earlier (Shabbat 55a and Moed Katan 16a).

Rashi on Shabbat 108b:12:6.english: A drop of cold [water] - To put in his eyes.

Rashi on Shabbat 108b:12:7.english: And washing hands and feet with hot water in the evening - [this] also brightens the eyes.

Rashi on Shabbat 108b:13:2.english: A hand to the eye - [That is,] in the morning, before one washes his hands.

Rashi on Shabbat 108b:13:3.hebrew: תיקצץ - נוח לו שתקצץ, שרוח רעה שורה על היד ומסמתו, וכן כולן:
Rashi on Shabbat 108b:13:3.english: Should be severed - It is better for him that it be severed, for an evil spirit rests upon the hand and blinds him, and similarly [for] all of them.

Rashi on Shabbat 108b:13:4.hebrew: לחסודה - ריבדא דכוסילתא, פלימא"ה בלע"ז:
Rashi on Shabbat 108b:13:4.english: To the chasudah - [This refers to] the bloodletting lancet, fleme [fleam] in Old French.

Rashi on Shabbat 108b:13:5.english: To the anus - The orifice of excrement, which is round like a ring.

Rashi on Shabbat 108b:13:6.english: Should be severed - And let it not touch the eye or the ear again before washing [one's hands].

Rashi on Shabbat 108b:1:1.english: But one may make, etc. - [This is] explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Shabbat 108b:1:2.hebrew: והלא הוא הילמי בין רב בין מעט - ואם המרובים אסורים, אף המועטים אסורים, ואם אלו מותרים, אף אלו מותרין. ובגמרא מפרש דלחומרא א"ר יוסי, דכולן לאיסור, מפני שהוא כמעבד — מתקן את האוכל הנתון לתוכו כדי שיתקיים:
Rashi on Shabbat 108b:1:2.english: But isn't it brine, whether much or little - If the large [quantities] are forbidden, the small [quantities] are also forbidden; and if these are permitted, those are also permitted. And in the Gemara it explains that Rabbi Yosei said [this] stringently, that all of them are forbidden, because he is like one who tans [hides] — preparing the food placed into it so that it will last.

Rashi on Shabbat 108b:1:3.hebrew: ואלו הן המותרין נותן שמן לתוך מים בתחלה - קודם שיתן המלח. נותן שמן לתוך המלח בתחלה, קודם שיתן המים, דהשמן מעכב שאין המלח מתערב יפה עם המים, ומתיש את כחו מהיות מי מלח עזין. אבל לא יתן מים ומלח תחילה, אפילו נותן שמן לבסוף, דבשעה שנותן מים ומלח יחד, הוא נראה כמעבד:
Rashi on Shabbat 108b:1:3.english: And these are the permitted [types of salt water]: one places oil into water initially - before he places the salt. [And] "one places oil into the salt initially" [means] before he places the water, for the oil prevents the salt from mixing well with the water and weakens its strength from becoming strong salt water. However, he may not place water and salt first, even if he places oil at the end, for at the moment he places water and salt together, he appears like one who is tanning.

Rashi on Shabbat 108b:2:1.english: What is [he] saying - What is brine and what is salt water?

Rashi on Shabbat 108b:3:1.english: To prohibit or to permit - [Regarding] this that he says both are equal: [is it] for prohibition or for permission?

Rashi on Shabbat 108b:4:1.english: Pickled [vegetables] - Vegetables that one pickles to preserve [them].

Rashi on Shabbat 108b:4:2.hebrew: גיסטרא - כלי שבור של חרס, ואינו ראוי לכל תשמיש כשלם, ומקצין אותו לכך:
Rashi on Shabbat 108b:4:2.english: Gistera - A broken earthenware vessel, which is not fit for every use like a whole [vessel], and they set it aside for that [purpose].

Rashi on Shabbat 108b:6:1.english: In which an egg floats - The strength of the salt prevents [it] from sinking.

Rashi on Shabbat 108b:7:2.hebrew: אין מולחין צנון וביצה - ג' וד' חתיכות יחד, שהמלח מעבדן ונעשין קשין, והוי תיקון:
Rashi on Shabbat 108b:7:2.english: One may not salt a radish or an egg - Three or four pieces together, because the salt cures them and they become firm, and it is [considered] fixing [them].

Rashi on Shabbat 108b:7:3.english: Initially, I would salt radishes - On Shabbat.

Rashi on Shabbat 108b:7:5.english: Piles - High mounds, round upon round.

Rashi on Shabbat 108b:7:6.english: Salting, I do not salt - two [pieces] together.

Rashi on Shabbat 108b:7:7.english: Dipping - At the time of eating, I dip [it in salt] and eat [it].

Rashi on Shabbat 108b:8:1.hebrew: קליפה חיצונה - דביצה היא החלבון, אלא איידי דתני בהדי אתרוג וצנון קליפה, נקט בה נמי לשון קליפה:
Rashi on Shabbat 108b:8:1.english: Outer peel - Of an egg, [this] is the white; however, since [the Tanna] taught "peel" alongside a citron and a radish, he also used the term "peel" for it.

Rashi on Shabbat 108b:8:2.english: They do not emerge from the intestines - For they bind together, harden, and are retained.

Rashi on Shabbat 108b:9:1.english: A person does not drown in the Sea of Sodom - Because the water is salty and the force of its saltiness prevents him from sinking.

Rashi on Shabbat 108b:9:2.english: And the statement is overturned - The things said about it are overturned.

Rashi on Shabbat 108b:9:3.english: A plank sinks?! - [This is said] as a rhetorical question.

Rashi on Shabbat 108b:9:4.hebrew: מהו למימשי מהני מיא גרסינן - מי אסור משום רפואה, דגזור רבנן בכל רפואות בשבת משום שחיקת סממנין, ואלו מרפאות את העין:
Rashi on Shabbat 108b:9:4.english: "What is [the ruling regarding] washing with this water" is our reading - Is it prohibited on account of healing, since the Rabbis decreed against all remedies on Shabbat on account of grinding medicines, and these [waters] heal the eye?

Rashi on Shabbat 108b:9:5.hebrew: שפיר דמי - דלאו מוכחא מילתא דלרפואה עביד. אף על פי שמרפאין, שרי, דטעמא דרפואה דאסירא ליתא אלא גזירה שמא ישחוק סממנין, דדמי לטחינה שהוא אב מלאכה:
Rashi on Shabbat 108b:9:5.english: It is well - Because it is not evident that he is doing [it] for healing. Even though [the waters] heal, it is permitted, for the reason that healing is prohibited is only a decree lest one grind herbs, which resembles grinding, which is a primary labor.
